objects.original: Two completed real Ito rows on one vector Brownian motion and a real weight W.
objects.reconstructed: Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. For n in N put t[n,i]=i*T/2^n for i=0,...,2^n, and Delta_i^n Z=Z(t[n,i+1])-Z(t[n,i]). A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(mu x lambda_T). I_T^j(eta) denotes the supplied completed continuous Ito process driven by the scalar coordinate B_j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j: the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic-integral approximations off their null uniform-Cauchy bad set, zero on that bad set, and held constant after T; at each t<=T it agrees almost everywhere with the L^2-completion integral up to t. Set X=A+sum_j I_T^j(eta_j), Y=C+sum_j I_T^j(xi_j). The integrand's toLp operation is its L^2 equivalence class represented by (omega,t)->eta(t,omega).
objects.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicWeightedCovariation.lean:16; X,Y explicitly use coordinateFamily hB for both rows; no independent substitute Brownian family.

domains.original: Finite measure, finite Brownian coordinate set, T>0 and usual filtration.
domains.reconstructed: Omega measurable; J finite with decidable equality; mu finite; R_+-filtration; T>0; vector B:R_+ x Omega->R^J; eta,xi indexed by J; A,C,W:R_+ x Omega->R.
domains.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicWeightedCovariation.lean:16; The full theorem binders contain finite mu, finite J, hT and hUsual.

quantifiers.original: All row data fixed; hypotheses for each deterministic slice and a.e. continuous paths; dyadic level tends to infinity.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universally all space and measure data, B and hypotheses, eta,xi,A,C,W; slice measurability of A,C,W; path assumptions of A,C,W. Then n->infinity.
quantifiers.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicWeightedCovariation.lean:16; The countable index K=(Sigma m,Fin(2^m+1))⊕Bool synchronizes all prefix and terminal-energy limits.

assumptions.original: Progressive product-L² diffusion rows; a.e. measurable continuous BV drifts; a.e. measurable weight slices and a.e. continuous weight paths.
assumptions.reconstructed: The vector Brownian hypothesis means B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments on finite families of pairwise disjoint half-open intervals are jointly independent; every continuous real linear functional ell sends B(t)-B(s), s<t, to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; paths are mu-almost surely continuous. B is strongly adapted, and for every s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of the sigma-algebra filtration(s). The filtration is right continuous, and every mu-null subset of Omega belongs to filtration(t) for every t>=0 (completeness at each time). eta_j,xi_j are progressive L^2 integrands on T. For each t<=T, the three slices A_t,C_t,W_t are mu-a.e. strongly measurable. A and C have continuous bounded-variation paths on [0,T] almost everywhere (separate statements); W has continuous paths there almost everywhere. No adaptedness or uniform deterministic bound on W is supplied.
assumptions.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicWeightedCovariation.lean:16; hAmeas,hCmeas,hWmeas,hA,hC,hW are exactly the source conditions; no hidden bound on W.

conclusion.original: Weighted products of simultaneous row increments tend in measure to integral W sum_j eta_j xi_j.
conclusion.reconstructed: The left-weighted sums sum_i W(t[n,i],omega)*Delta_i^n X(omega)*Delta_i^n Y(omega) converge in mu-measure as n->infinity to integral_0^T W(s,omega)*sum_j eta_j(s,omega)*xi_j(s,omega) ds.
conclusion.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicWeightedCovariation.lean:16; The final application of tendsto_dyadic_weighted_sums_of_prefix_limits uses b=sum eta*xi.

scopes.original: Only a fixed-horizon in-measure limit; W need not be adapted or deterministically bounded.
scopes.reconstructed: One terminal horizon T is fixed. Convergence is in measure, not claimed in L^1, almost surely, or uniformly over terminal times. Weights are evaluated at left endpoints; products use full adjacent increments.
scopes.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicWeightedCovariation.lean:16; hSm supplies measurability and the subsequence criterion returns convergence in measure, not a.s. full-sequence convergence.

constant_dependencies.original: No deterministic bound on W or variation is assumed.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: No quantitative constant is stated; samplewise continuity permits sample-dependent bounds but no deterministic one is hypothesized. All data may influence convergence.
